```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```
```{r}
# Load all necessary libraries for the assignment
library(caret)
library(dplyr)
library(e1071)
```
```{r}
# Load the assignment dataset
bank <- read.csv("UniversalBank.csv")
```
```{r}
# Partition the data and Split the data into 60% training and 40% validation sets
set.seed(1)
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(bank$Personal.Loan, p = 0.6, list = FALSE)
train <- bank[trainIndex, ]
valid <- bank[-trainIndex, ]
```
```{r}
# A. Create pivot table with Online as column, CreditCard as row, Loan as secondary row
pivot_table <- table(train$CreditCard, train$Online, train$Personal.Loan)

# View the pivot table in flat format
ftable(pivot_table)
```
```{r}
# B. Probability of Loan = 1 given CC = 1 and Online = 1
cc1_online1_loan1 <- pivot_table["1", "1", "1"]
cc1_online1_total <- sum(pivot_table["1", "1", ])

# Compute conditional probability of loan
prob_loan_given_cc1_online1 <- cc1_online1_loan1 / cc1_online1_total
prob_loan_given_cc1_online1 #probability of loan acceptance
```
```{r}
# C. Create separate pivot tables for Loan/Online and Loan/CC
loan_online <- table(train$Personal.Loan, train$Online)
loan_cc <- table(train$Personal.Loan, train$CreditCard)
loan_online #output of loan and online
loan_cc #output of loan and credit card
```
```{r}
# D. Compute conditional probabilities of each scenario
# -------------------------------
# i. P(CC = 1 | Loan = 1)
p_cc_given_loan1 <- mean(train$CreditCard[train$Personal.Loan == 1])
p_cc_given_loan1
```
```{r}
# ii. P(Online = 1 | Loan = 1)
p_online_given_loan1 <- mean(train$Online[train$Personal.Loan == 1])
p_online_given_loan1
```
```{r}
# iii. P(Loan = 1)
p_loan1 <- mean(train$Personal.Loan == 1)
p_loan1
```
```{r}
# iv. P(CC = 1 | Loan = 0)
p_cc_given_loan0 <- mean(train$CreditCard[train$Personal.Loan == 0])
p_cc_given_loan0
```
```{r}
# v. P(Online = 1 | Loan = 0)
p_online_given_loan0 <- mean(train$Online[train$Personal.Loan == 0])
p_online_given_loan0
```
```{r}
# vi. P(Loan = 0)
p_loan0 <- mean(train$Personal.Loan == 0)
p_loan0
```
```{r}
# E Naive Bayes probability where P(Loan = 1 | CC = 1, Online = 1)
#Apply Naive Bayes logic
numerator <- p_cc_given_loan1 * p_online_given_loan1 * p_loan1
denominator <- numerator + (p_cc_given_loan0 * p_online_given_loan0 * p_loan0)

naive_bayes_prob <- numerator / denominator
naive_bayes_prob
```
```{r}
# F Compare with pivot probability > which is more accurate?
comparison <- data.frame(
  PivotTable = prob_loan_given_cc1_online1,
  NaiveBayes = naive_bayes_prob
)
print(comparison)
```
```{r}
#Analysis of F: pivot table (empirical estimate) has a higher probability and is therefore more accurate than NaiveBayes which may over/understimate the true probability 

# G. Run Naive Bayes model and predict for CC = 1, Online = 1; Prepare training data for model
train_nb <- train %>% select(Personal.Loan, CreditCard, Online)
train_nb$Personal.Loan <- as.factor(train_nb$Personal.Loan)
```
```{r}
# Fit the Naive Bayes model
model_nb <- naiveBayes(Personal.Loan ~ CreditCard + Online, data = train_nb)
model_nb
```
```{r}
# Predict the probability for customer where CreditCard = 1 and Online = 1
predict(model_nb, data.frame(CreditCard = 1, Online = 1), type = "raw")
#Output from G is higher on non-accptance (0) than output from E (0.09055), but lower than acceptance (1)
```
